questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. The speedometer in a car consists of a pointer which rotates. The pointer is situated several millimetres from a calibrated scale. What could cause a random error in the driver’s measurement of the car’s speed?

options.A: The car’s speed is affected by the wind direction.
options.B: The driver’s eye is not always in the same position in relation to the pointer.
options.C: The speedometer does not read zero when the car is at rest.

questions.questionText: In an experiment to demonstrate Brownian motion, smoke particles in a container are illuminated by a strong light source and observed through a microscope. The particles are seen as small specks of light that are in motion. What causes the Brownian motion?

options.A: collisions between the smoke particles and air molecules
options.B: collisions between the smoke particles and the walls of the container
options.C: convection currents within the air as it is warmed by the light source
options.D: kinetic energy gained by the smoke particles on absorption of light Space for working
